Built-in water ant moat; optional solar panel adds a second moat on the hanger
AI recognition of 150+ hummingbird species, free in the Birdfy app

products.returns: 30 days from receipt on birdfy.com; buyer pays return shipping unless the unit is defective
products.summary: A single-camera hummingbird feeder with a built-in ant moat, a 9,000 mAh battery and free species ID. The cheapest of the three main camera hummingbird feeders and the only one under 150 dollars with an ant moat.
products.fit: First camera hummingbird feeder, especially if ants or a monthly fee are your worry. Also the lightest and simplest to hang.
caveats: 1080p video at 20 fps, not 2K; Bird Buddy's Pro takes sharper stills.
No motion sensitivity setting; a feeder swinging in wind can create empty clips.
Without the optional solar panel, heavy traffic (about 200 visits a day) meant recharging every 3 days in one review.
2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; the feeder needs Wi-Fi to record and upload.

products.name: Birdfy Hum Feeder Duo Dual-Camera Hummingbird Feeder, 2K, 20 fl oz
specs: Two cameras, 2048 × 1536 at 25 fps; 1024 × 768 at 120 fps slow motion on the main camera
5,000 mAh lithium-ion, USB charging (5 V / 2 A); solar panel optional
AI recognition of hummingbird species, free in the Birdfy app
Auto-recorded clips kept 30 days free; no microSD slot; no night vision
products.returns: 30 days from receipt on birdfy.com; buyer pays return shipping unless the unit is defective
products.summary: The only hummingbird feeder with two cameras, so you get a front view and a side profile of the same visit, plus a 20 fl oz tank that needs fewer refills than the 14 fl oz feeders.
products.fit: Busy feeders with several hummingbirds, and anyone who wants 2K video from two angles without a subscription.
caveats: No motion sensitivity setting; one reviewer logged many empty clips on windy days.
Reviews mention the side camera fogging and nectar leaking if the base is not seated properly after refilling.
Smaller 5,000 mAh battery than the single-camera Hum Feeder; plan on the solar panel for a busy feeder.

notes:
QUERY CHOICE: 'best hummingbird feeder with camera' returns mostly keyword-stuffed affiliate pages and store listings; no page compares ant moats, battery and subscription side by side. Birdfy sells the only sub-150-dollar camera hummingbird feeder with a built-in ant moat and the only dual-camera one.

PAIN POINTS (source mentions): ants reaching nectar / no moat on Bird Buddy (4: MacRumors, Bird Buddy FAQ, Birdfy ant guide, Netvue listing); empty or missed clips (5: Gear Diary Duo review 'lot of empty video clips, no sensitivity setting', a review logging 277 detections in one windy day, Bob Vila on Bird Buddy 10-min cooldown missing visits, MacRumors 'does not record every visit', Trustpilot 'sees hummingbird but nothing recorded'); battery drain without solar (4: Bob Vila Birdfy every 3 days at ~200 visits/day, MacRumors Bird Buddy weekly in shade, Twice about a week, Thingtesting 'short battery'); Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz and setup (4: Bob Vila setup snag, Best Buy reviewer, Walmart 'inconsistent', Twice); subscription needed for automatic ID on Bird Buddy (3: Bird Buddy shop page, Digital Camera World snippet, Bob Vila); lid / leaks on Birdfy (2: Chewy review, Duo listing review); Duo side camera fogging (1).

SEGMENTS: (1) first camera feeder / ants / no fee -> Birdfy Hum Feeder, 129.99 vs Bird Buddy Pro 249, moat built in, free ID. (2) best image quality -> Bird Buddy Pro honestly wins (5 MP stills, 2K HDR); stated in lead. (3) busy feeder, two angles -> Birdfy Hum Feeder Duo (only dual-cam, 20 fl oz). (4) fewest refills -> FeatherSnap 1 L.
